title: Canonicalize TensorView axes without a transient name map
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView construction bounded and froze tensor.axes, then built a complete axis-name-to-axis dictionary solely to reject duplicate names and recover canonical name order. That transient map duplicated the already-retained bounded axis records, introduced unnecessary hashing, and rebuilt even an exact tuple that was already canonical.
primary_claim: TensorView now validates axis records while tracking whether their existing name order is already nondecreasing. An exact canonical tuple is retained directly. Noncanonical input uses the existing deterministic name sort, and duplicate axis names are rejected by adjacent comparison after canonicalization. Axis hashing is no longer required for constructor canonicalization.
gardener_decision: Use the axis tuple's mandatory canonical ordering itself for validation and duplicate detection rather than maintaining a second name map. Preserve deterministic sorting only as the fallback for noncanonical input, and reuse an already-canonical exact tuple by identity.
acceptance: constructor axis canonicalization does not require hashing every axis name into a transient dictionary
an exact already-canonical tuple of TensorAxis records is retained by identity
unsorted axes remain deterministically canonicalized by axis name
duplicate axis names remain fail-closed after canonicalization
